title: 2025 hand case: joint, wages $120,000, 2 children and 1 other dependant, itemizes

source.where: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025): Schedule A, Child Tax Credit; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 3

note: AGI 120,000 - 1,000 student loan interest = 119,000. Itemized: state and local 4,800 + 3,000 = 7,800 (under the 40,000 cap); mortgage 20,000; charity 5,000 (2025 has no 0.5% floor); medical 15,000 - 7.5% x 119,000 (8,925) = 6,075. Total 38,875 over the 31,500 standard. Taxable 80,125. Tax 10% x 23,850 = 2,385 + 12% x 56,275 = 6,753 = 9,138. Credits: 2 x 2,200 + 500 = 4,900. Total 4,238. Paid 10,000; refund 5,762.

title: 2025 hand case: single, wages $190,000 over the wage base, self-employment $40,000, interest $6,000

source.where: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025); Schedule SE (wage base $176,100); Forms 8959 and 8960

note: Allowed rounding of a cent: Wages already pass the 176,100 Social Security wage base, so self-employment tax is only Medicare: 92.35% x 40,000 = 36,940 x 2.9% = 1,071.26; half 535.63. Additional Medicare: (190,000 + 36,940 - 200,000) = 26,940 x 0.9% = 242.46. AGI = 236,000 - 535.63 = 235,464.37; NIIT = 3.8% x min(6,000, 35,464.37) = 228.00.

title: 2025 hand case: single, wages $20,000, one child: the refundable part of the credit

source.where: Instructions for Schedule 8812 (2025): the refundable part is the smaller of the unused credit, $1,700 and 15% of earned income over $2,500

note: Taxable 20,000 - 15,750 = 4,250; tax 10% = 425. The credit 2,200 uses 425 of it; the unused 1,775 is capped at 1,700 (15% x 17,500 = 2,625 is larger).
